For RE, pre-screening type pairs in the upper SCS quartile identifies confusability risk (3--5\,pp expected impact). \paragraph{Practical implications.}
For RE, pre-screening type pairs in the upper SCS quartile identifies confusability risk (3--5\,pp expected impact). For NER, reducing candidate types per prompt is the primary lever, as confusability-aware batching provides no additional benefit. Schema partitioning remains non-viable due to merge amplification (NER) and routing uncertainty (RE). We suggest four actionable directions: (1)~practitioners may flag type pairs with SCS${}\,>\,0.85$ as high-confusion-risk indicators for targeted evaluation or contrastive few-shot examples; label renaming alone is counterproductive due to unfamiliarity effects (Appendix~\ref{app:renaming}); (2)~for RE batches, monitoring mean BCS provides a lightweight quality indicator, since BCS explains 22--53\% of cross-batch variance; (3)~contrastive definitions or targeted few-shot examples for high-SCS pairs may reduce confusion without the label-unfamiliarity penalty of renaming (untested; future work); (4)~evaluation should report schema-controlled metrics alongside aggregate scores, as performance gaps between low- and high-BCS batches can reach 25--31\,pp.
